newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas down sharply on weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas down sharply on weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were sharply lower Monday, pressured by milder temperatures and storage withdrawals in the East, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for Tuesday delivery fell an average of 40 cents to about C$2.70 per gigajoule (GJ), with deals reported done in the C$2.60-2.90 range.
"There's a little excess gas in the market," one Calgary-based trader said, adding that milder temperatures are forecast to continue over the next few days.
February AECO prices were talked in the C$2.80-2.85 per GJ area, about 50 cents higher than January indices.
At Sumas, Wash., prices lost about 40 cents to the $2.41-2.46 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range. Early deals were reported done at $2.50.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest are forecast to remain near-normal throughout this week.
At Niagara, prices began as high as $3.60 per mmBtu but quickly eroded to a low of $3.15. Traders said most deals were done in the $3.35-3.40 area.

"The market is really quiet. People normally in the market just weren't there," one Calgary-based marketer said, noting plentiful storage supplies in the East might be keeping buyers away from the spot market.
The Canadian Gas Association said Friday that as of January 10, stocks in the East were 142.12 billion cubic feet, or 61.11 percent full, compared with 43.50 percent full a year ago.
However, stocks in the West continue to lag behind year-ago levels at 46.72 percent full, versus 56.70 percent full a year ago.
